lots.what_it_is: Filigree panel belt, Tibetan/Himalayan style: diamond-shaped floral filigree panels on ring-and-bar links, square rope-edged buckle plate with two snow lions under a jewel/lotus motif and Tibetan script above and below, rear hook clasp. Gowans: 'Unmarked Tibetan 97% silver ceremonial belt, 363.3g, 95cm'. Current bid $500 (1 bid) at 30/09/2026.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The researcher found no entries (search budget exhausted, and it was still exhausted for me). The only Denhams belts I saw (Japanese Meiji mon-charm belt 112g GBP 150 Feb 2026; Edwardian Birmingham 1903 belt 178g GBP 135 Oct 2025) are different items and are not used. Metal reference only, not a comp: Perth Mint silver ask AUD 88.54/oz (page opened 30 Sep 2026) = AUD 2.847/g fine. If the 97% claim is right, 363.3g x 0.97 = 352.4g fine = about AUD 1,003 at spot, perhaps AUD 800-900 from a scrap buyer. The researcher's AUD 1.5/g figure was wrong (too low).
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep and flip maxima are 0. Context only: all-in at the current $500 bid is $599 (500 x 1.198). Melt at spot if 97% silver is about AUD 1,003, so the current bid is under melt only if the purity claim holds. If it were sterling-grade or lower, or partly white metal, the floor falls fast (at 80% silver about AUD 830 at spot, and nothing if it is white metal). Purity is the whole question.
lots.confidence_reason: No marks (Gowans itself says unmarked), 97% is a seller assertion with no test stated, and no market evidence at all.
lots.key_photo_findings: Re-checked all 4 photos. Photo 2: buckle plate with two snow lions facing a central jewel/lotus motif, Tibetan-script bands top and bottom (not read), rosette bosses at the corners, rope-twist border. Photo 3: repeating diamond panels with stamped floral centres and wire scroll filigree. Photo 4 close-up: lumpy hand-soldered joins with pink/purple discolouration round the solder, which looks like firescale (a copper-bearing alloy) or flux residue, not typical of near-fine silver. No hallmark or purity stamp visible anywhere. Workmanship is serviceable rather than fine; looks like 20th century export or tourist work, not demonstrably antique.
lots.condition: Complete as photographed; general tarnish in recesses, some bent link joins, crude solder repairs with discolouration. Back of buckle and clasp not shown.
lots.dropped_entries: None to drop: the researcher returned no entries. I discarded the researcher's AUD 1.5/g silver figure, which understates today's price by nearly half.
lots.question_for_gowans: How was the 97% figure established (XRF or acid test, and on which parts)? Is the buckle plate solid or backed/filled? Can you photograph the back of the buckle and the hook clasp, and confirm no parts are base metal?
lots.identification_check: Identification as a Himalayan-style filigree belt confirmed; metal content not confirmable from photos.
